item.title: Four suspects in custody after drug raids in Solovi, Legalega and Lautoka
item.description: Four suspects remain in police custody following separate raids in Solovi, Lautoka and Legalega, which resulted in the seizure of suspected drugs and ammunition. Nadi Police arrested two men during a raid in Solovi late last night, where plastic bags containing white crystals believed to be drugs and ammunition were seized.
item.content:encoded:
Four suspects remain in police custody following separate raids in Solovi, Lautoka and Legalega, which resulted in the seizure of suspected drugs and ammunition.

Nadi Police arrested two men during a raid in Solovi late last night, where plastic bags containing white crystals believed to be drugs and ammunition were seized.

Police say one of the suspects has a previous history of involvement in drug-related activities.

In a separate operation in Lautoka, a joint taskforce comprising police and military officers seized plastic bags containing white substances and green leaves believed to be marijuana.

The suspect was taken into custody as investigations continue.

Another raid conducted by the joint taskforce in Legalega also resulted in positive finds.

Police say all four suspects remain in custody while the seized substances are sent for analysis.

Police says the seized ammunition will be handed over to the Republic of Fiji Military Forces for inspection.

Members of the public are urged to report crimes, provide tips or share information about suspicious activities by calling 1681.

Photos and videos can also be sent via WhatsApp, Viber or Signal to 9905922 .

item.title: National Referendum Bill passed unanimously with rules for referendum process
item.description: Rashika Kumar , Mikaele Liga · 02/10/2026 While speaking during the debate on the Bill, Opposition MP Premila Kumar claimed that people will experience a referendum for the last time if that Constitution goes through.
item.content:encoded:
Rashika Kumar , Mikaele Liga · 02/10/2026

While speaking during the debate on the Bill, Opposition MP Premila Kumar claimed that people will experience a referendum for the last time if that Constitution goes through.

She also says too many fundamental rules are left to regulations that have not been presented to Parliament.

Kumar says these rules will determine how campaigns operate, how money is raised and spent, what information voters receive and how results can be challenged.

She also citizens should not have to work out their referendum rights and offences from a combination of two Acts and subsequent administrative decisions.

Kumar questioned the reliance on newspapers to communicate important information, calling for wider use of SMS, social media, radio, television and the official Elections Office website.

Despite supporting the Bill, Opposition MP Jone Usamate says this Government appears to be paying lip service to participatory democracy as the Constitution being proposed does not provide for referendums and is entirely based on representative democracy.

Usamate also says the Parliamentary Standing Committee of Justice, Law and Human Rights waited five months, from April to September, for a revised draft, leaving insufficient time to incorporate relevant Electoral Act provisions directly into the Bill.

He further says campaign spending limits and guidelines ensuring equal airtime for supporters and opponents have not been adequately addressed.

Responding to Kumar's claim about future referendums, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka stresses this will not be the only referendum we will ever have in Fiji.

He says she is correct in relation to Section 160 of the 2013 Constitution, because there will be no corresponding section 160 in the proposed new Constitution.

However, Rabuka says the Bill also allows Parliament to pass a resolution declaring that an issue or matter is of sufficient national importance to be submitted to voters for their views.

He adds future Parliaments may decide to take questions to the people.

Rabuka says the Bill affirms a democratic belief that has united free societies for generations, on questions touching the constitutional future of a nation, the people themselves must have a voice.

The Prime Minister says on other matters, the Government may still seek people's views through a referendum, although the result would not be binding on the Government.

Minister for Information Lynda Tabuya says the Bill will strengthen the process and civil participation.

Tabuya says the Bill will provide the need for conflict resolution mechanisms instead of a really strong emphasis on creating offences and applying offences.

item.title: CJ Temo and CR Bainivalu remain silent after 2 cases of missing cocaine amounting to $50M
item.description: Chief Justice, Salesi Temo and Chief Registrar, Tomasi Bainivalu remain silent after the two cases of breaches at the Suva High Court Exhibit Room which has resulted in the disappearance of $50 million of cocaine from March to this month. fijivillage News has asked the Chief Justice and Chief Registrar what steps are being taken to ensure the person involved in taking the drugs from the exhibit ro
item.content:encoded:
Chief Justice, Salesi Temo and Chief Registrar, Tomasi Bainivalu remain silent after the two cases of breaches at the Suva High Court Exhibit Room which has resulted in the disappearance of $50 million of cocaine from March to this month.

fijivillage News has asked the Chief Justice and Chief Registrar what steps are being taken to ensure the person involved in taking the drugs from the exhibit room is apprehended.

We have also asked why the CCTV cameras were not operational and who was providing security at the exhibit room.

fijivillage News has also asked whether a full audit will be done for all the court exhibit rooms and whether all the drug exhibits will be tested.

All questions are being referred to Police.

The Police Forensics Team was at the court house today conducting investigations.

item.title: Counter-Narcotics Bill passed, Bureau to lead Fiji’s fight against drugs
item.description: Priya Nand , Mansi Chand · 01/10/2026 Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran says the proposed legislation is fundamentally a child-protection, violence-prevention and family-strengthening measure, and a vital shield for social protection.
item.content:encoded:
Priya Nand , Mansi Chand · 01/10/2026

Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran says the proposed legislation is fundamentally a child-protection, violence-prevention and family-strengthening measure, and a vital shield for social protection.

Kiran says the Bill looks at the human reality behind the drug crisis and provides legislative tools needed to protect Fiji’s most vulnerable citizens.

She says a transformative feature of the framework is Clause 5, which formally defines a vulnerable and at-risk person.

Kiran says for the first time in Fiji’s legal history, the narcotics framework explicitly recognises that children, people experiencing extreme poverty, the homeless and those facing mental health challenges require targeted protection rather than blanket criminalisation.

She says Clause 80 creates serious criminal offences for any adult who sells, supplies or administers drugs to a child, or procures a child for illicit drug activities.

Kiran says Clause 81 goes further by placing a legal obligation on adults to protect children in their care from exposure to illicit substances.

Meanwhile, Opposition MP Alvick Maharaj says the Bill represents a turning point in Fiji’s fight against illicit drugs by providing a comprehensive framework to dismantle supply networks while protecting and rehabilitating people affected by substance abuse.

Maharaj says Fiji is no longer dealing solely with localised marijuana cultivation but is battling syndicates using Fiji as a hub for hard drugs.

He says the scale of the drug crisis has grown from a domestic law-enforcement issue into a multi-billion-dollar transnational threat that requires an unprecedented response.

Assistant Minister in the Office of the Prime Minister Sakiusa Tubuna says under Clause 13, the proposed framework will go beyond simply investigating drug offences.

Tubuna says its responsibilities will include preventing and controlling the supply and demand of illicit drugs, investigating related and transnational organised crime, developing prevention strategies, supporting treatment and rehabilitation, cooperating with other agencies and international partners, and maintaining a national database on drug trafficking, abuse and money laundering.

He says the Bill recognises that the drug problem cannot be fought by Police alone and provides for cooperation with agencies including Immigration, the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service, Biosecurity, maritime and aviation authorities and the Financial Intelligence Unit.

Tubuna says one of the most important aspects of the Bill is that it does not treat every person affected by drugs simply as a criminal.

He says there must be a clear distinction between those who profit from trafficking and exploiting people and those who have become trapped by addiction.

Tubuna says the Bill provides for prevention, early intervention, public education, school awareness, community outreach, treatment, rehabilitation, counselling, aftercare and reintegration.

Minister for Sports Jese Saukuru says the fight against illicit drugs is not simply a fight against substances but a fight to protect human potential, children, families, communities and Fiji’s future.

Saukuru says a young person who has made a mistake should not be written off and should instead be provided with a pathway back to family, education, employment, sport and society.

He says young people must grow up understanding respect, consent, responsibility and the dignity of every human being.
